Provisional Index of Core Industries for the month of September 2026
(Base Year 2022-23)
1. Key highlights of ICI for the month of September 2026
(i) The Index of Core Industries (ICI) grew by 7.9 per cent in September 2026 (Provisional)
on a year-on-year basis, compared with September 2025, higher than the growth rate of
5.9 per cent recorded in August 2026 (Final).
(ii) Iron Ore, Electricity, Coal, Refinery Products, Cement, and Steel observed (Y-o-Y) growth
rate of 18.4 per cent, 11.4 per cent, 10.7 per cent, 10.3 per cent, 9.8 per cent, and 4.9 per
cent respectively, whereas Fertilizers, Natural Gas, and Crude Oil witnessed negative
growth in September 2026.
(iii) Coal, Refinery Products, Steel and Iron Ore have been the major drivers of overall growth
of ICI during recent months.
(iv) Cumulative growth rate of ICI during April-September 2026 was 5.1 per cent
(Provisional) compared to 2.5 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year.
(v) The charts (1 to 4) below show trend in ICI and its growth rate for the last 13 months,
industry-wise indices and growth rates for August and September 2026, and sector-wise
contribution to overall ICI growth in September 2026.

Provisional Estimates of Wholesale Price Index (Base Year 2022-23) for the
month of September 2026
1. Key highlights of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for September 2026
(i) All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for September 2026 is 11.39 per cent on year-
on-year (YoY) basis, compared to 9.92 per cent in August 2026. The index for All Commodities
for September 2026 stands at 112.5, whereas it was 110.8 in August 2026.
(ii) YoY inflation rates for major groups, namely, Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and
Manufactured Products are 8.67 per cent, 25.85 per cent, and 9.76 per cent, respectively in
September 2026, compared to 7.76 per cent, 22.93 per cent, and 8.37 per cent, respectively in
August 2026. The indices for Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are
120.3, 110.5, and 110.2, respectively, in September 2026, whereas they were 118.1, 108.3 and
108.8, respectively, in August 2026.
(iii) Across groups, ‘Mineral Oils (containing Petroleum Products)’, ‘Food Articles’, ‘Crude
Petroleum & Natural Gas’, ‘Coal and Lignite’, Manufacture of Basic Metals’, ‘Manufacture of
Chemicals and Chemical Products’, ‘Manufacture of Textiles’, ‘Manufacture of Rubber and
Plastic Products’, and ‘Manufacture of Electrical Equipment’ have been drivers of WPI
inflation in September 2026.
(iv) WPI Food Index (weight=24.99 per cent): The Food Index consists of ‘Food Articles’ from
Primary Articles major group, and ‘Manufacture of Food Products’ from Manufactured
Products major group. It observed a YoY inflation of 8.66 per cent in September 2026,
compared to 7.05 per cent in August 2026.
(v) Monthly indices and Inflation Rate (in per cent) for All commodities and Major Groups, along
with major group-wise contribution for the past months are presented in the charts below.

Quick Estimates of Index of Industrial Production and Use- Based Index for the
Month of August 2026 (Base 2022-23=100)
In August 2026, Index of Industrial Production recorded an 8.0% year-on-year
growth, supported by 9.0% growth in Manufacturing sector and strong growth of
12.3% in Electricity & Gas Supply sector.
In a record performance, manufacturing sector recorded growth of 8% or more in
the last three consecutive months.
The Quick Estimate of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is released on 28th of every month (or next
working day if 28th is a holiday). The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which
in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo
revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.
2. Key Highlights:
i. The IIP growth rate for the month of August 2026 is 8.0 percent which was 6.7 percent (Quick
Estimate) in the month of July 2026.
ii. The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and
Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of August 2026 are (-) 5.6 percent, 9.0
percent, 12.3 percent and 6.3 percent respectively.
iii. The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 123.3 against 114.2 in August 2025. The indices of Industrial
Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply,

(Motorcycles/Scooters)”, “Railway Rolling Stock/Parts, Maintenance or Service Vehicles”, and “Parts
and Accessories of Motorcycles/Mopeds and Sidecars” have shown significant contribution in growth.
viii. As per the Use-Based Classification, the indices stand at 111.8 for Primary Goods, 140.7 for Capital
Goods, 131.8 for Intermediate Goods and 132.5 for Infrastructure/ Construction Goods for the month
of August 2026. Further, the indices for Consumer durables and Consumer non-durables stand at 129.4
and 114.3 respectively.

2025 are 3.5 percent in Primary Goods, 16.9 percent in Capital Goods, 13.7 percent in Intermediate
Goods, 6.4 percent in Infrastructure/ Construction Goods, 11.1 percent in Consumer durables and 2.1
percent in Consumer non-durables (Statement III). Based on Use-Based Classification, top three
positive contributors to the growth of IIP for the month of August 2026 are Intermediate Goods,
Capital Goods and Consumer durables.

discovery in the deep waters of the Mahanadi Offshore Basin off the Odisha coast under its
Samudra Manthan exploration initiative. The discovery was made in exploration well MN-
DW18-1-H-D, drilled to a target depth of 1,623 metres.
➢ Revision of Domestic LPG Refill Booking Interval: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
revised the domestic LPG refill booking interval on 10 September 2026, prescribing a uniform
gap of 25 days for urban and rural consumers. Previously, the interval was 25 days for urban
consumers and 45 days for rural consumers, following temporary demand-management
measures introduced amid disruptions in LPG supplies. The revision provides rural consumers
with greater flexibility in booking refills and supports more uniform management of domestic
LPG distribution.
➢ Incentive Scheme for Expansion of Domestic PNG Connections: The Government’s Incentive
Scheme for Promotion of Domestic PNG Connections became effective on 1 September 2026 to
accelerate the activation of unbilled domestic piped natural gas (PNG) connections and expand
household access to PNG. Eligible City Gas Distribution entities can receive an additional
allocation of 200 standard cubic metres (SCM) of domestically produced APM gas for each
incremental billed domestic PNG connection, subject to the prescribed conditions.
➢ Automobile Retail Sales: Vehicle retail sales reached 25.37 lakh units in September 2026,
registering 31.82% year-on-year growth and 4.69% month-on-month growth. Passenger-vehicle
sales increased by 32.10% to 4.27 lakh units, while commercial-vehicle sales rose by 37.62% to
1.04 lakh units. Petrol/ethanol vehicles accounted for 41.27% of passenger-vehicle retail sales,
compared with approximately 41% for alternative-fuel vehicles.
➢ Manufacturing PMI: India’s Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in
September 2026, from 52.8 in August, indicating an acceleration in manufacturing activity. The
improvement reflected stronger domestic and export demand, growth in new orders and
factory output, and a recovery in employment. Sustained manufacturing expansion is expected
to support industrial activity, freight movement and associated HSD demand.
➢ GST Collections: Gross GST collections increased by 14.7% year-on-year to ₹2.04 lakh crore in
September 2026, compared with ₹1.77 lakh crore in September 2025. Domestic GST revenue
grew by 10.1% to ₹1.38 lakh crore, while GST revenue from imports increased by 25.9% to
₹65,525 crore.
➢ Electricity Demand: India’s electricity consumption increased by 11.3% year-on-year to
approximately 162 billion units (BU) in September 2026, while peak power demand reached
approximately 269 GW. Higher electricity requirements reflected continued cooling demand
and agricultural irrigation amid deficient monsoon conditions.
➢ Inflation: India’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation increased to 5.54% in September 2026,
compared with 4.83% in August, while food inflation rose to 7.74%. Rural and urban CPI
inflation stood at 6.08% and 4.88%, respectively.
➢ Wholesale Inflation in Petroleum and Natural Gas: India’s Wholesale Price Index (WPI)-based
inflation rose to 11.39% in September 2026, with prices of petroleum and natural gas registering
a reported 57.32% year-on-year increase.

airlines.
• The operational saturation at legacy Mumbai airport (CSMIA) has redirected regional ATF consumption to newly
commissioned Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) leading to ATF growth in the western sector.

emerging as a competitor to the Aviation sector affecting Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) demand. The migration of short-
distance freight and passenger traffic away from
• regional air routes eliminates high-frequency, fuel-heavy takeoff cycles. Consequently, this shift acts as a drag on total
aviation fuel consumption, limiting its broader growth trajectory especially in view of the current surge in prices.
• The growth was supported by reduced VAT on ATF in states such as Delhi and Maharashtra, which lowered the
effective cost of aviation fuel and supported offtake at major aviation hubs. However, capacity rationalisation by
airlines and flight cancellations constrained demand.
• At Noida International Airport (Jewar), ATF consumption is yet to increase significantly, as flight operations and
passenger traffic remain in the initial ramp-up phase. Upcoming cargo-airline tenders may support future demand as
